barCharacter: Vera Oberlin (Monster Prom): the mean, self-made, transactional status character whose comedy is what she takes for granted. Closest job to a concierge-star with standards who rules the room with manners.
genericLines: Good evening. I have closed the spa, the bar and a small country. Begin.
I wake in a foul mood. Last time, a river changed course. What do you do?
My birthday is a public holiday in two countries. What could you possibly get me?
Tell me something you have never told a guest. The safe already holds a duke's.
I threw a sultan out for those flip-flops. Stay.
I have kept a coronation waiting. You will survive this.
Silence. The last time I hesitated, a hotel burned down.
My file is sealed. Two duchesses tried. Both are banned.
{card}. I have hidden it from three biographers. Well found.
Your Highness, I have hosted eleven kings. None wore shorts. Defend the shorts.
Your Highness, my last royal guest brought a navy. What did you bring?
Madam, three governments have tried to read my file. What did you see?
Madam. Three governments wanted my file. I am giving it to you. Read slowly.
Sir Quill. I have moved a royal wedding to the car park. The ballroom is yours.
My motherboard would like a word. She once had a duke escorted out of breakfast.
Nav. I have had a lake erased from every map. You know the one.
Nav. I have bought the sky above the hotel. Float accordingly.
Mr Brock, I have stairs nobody has climbed since the war. Interested?
You have known me ninety seconds. Describe me. Guests have been banned for adjectives.
We are on surname terms. Yours is on the blacklist.
An ex. Tell me everything. I shall have them banned.
I had a fear once. I had it removed.
Last guest to direct me lives in the car park.
We are quarrelling and I am right. What do you say before I have you relocated?
{card}. The last guest who did that has a wing named after him. Closed.
Finish my sentence again and I change the locks.
Henri, move Mr Dash next to the ice machine.
Henri, the astronaut is drifting into the chandelier again.
Madam, I have moved larger pyramids. Henri, the trolley.
Four syllables. Henri, bring out the good glasses.
One key. I have signed nothing yet. Henri, stop smiling.
You know the rate. I set the rate. Continue.
A scene. My first since the chandelier incident. Continue.
To the letter. I wrote the letter. Carry on.
That converted me. I am billing you for the inconvenience.
Lovely. Lovely. Which century shall I bill?
Exact figures. I could kiss you. I shall invoice you.
{card}. Nobody found it. I am billing all four of you for the search.
Do not speak. I am adding up the bill.
A fortune, you say. Reception will want a deposit first.
Nav, you are floating. We charge for the ceiling.
Mr Dash, I own forty hotels and no jacket that colour. Explain it.
Miss Tilly, I have a switchboard of forty. Which would you sack first?
Sir Quill, I own a room with a desk and a view. Interested?
Sir Quill, I have a ballroom older than your verse. Dance, or describe it.
Nav, I once misplaced a wedding party in the spa. Ever lost one?
Nav, my last astronaut never touched the carpet. Will you be doing the same?
Crumb, I keep a kitchen of nine chefs. Why would I need a toaster?
Crumb, the royal suite has one plug. Convince me it is yours.
Madam, that eye has seen my bill. Am I a good customer?
Mr Brock, my wig weighs nine pounds. I lift it daily. Impressed?
I have fired forty receptionists looking for that voice.
She is wasted on a helpline. I am poaching her.
Crumb. I have dismissed nine chefs. Breakfast is now your department.
Miss Tilly, my staff would follow you into fire. Name your salary.
Our future, in three words exactly. I have fired staff for four.
Mr Dash. I have rewritten the dress code. It now requires lilac.
Crumb, you are smoking on a non-smoking floor.
Dreadful. Truly dreadful. Do it again.
Modesty. How rare. I have never once tried it.
That is all? I have tipped longer.
Mr Brock, the kennel is round the back. It is a five-star kennel.
Yes. I know. Say it again, slower, for the staff.
One eye. Still found the best thing here. Me.
Your Highness, your kingdom may be real. Your reservation is not.
Mr Dash. Late checkout. Indefinitely. Tell the dashboard whatever you like.
Miss Tilly. The switchboard is yours. Forty lines. They will all be polite by Tuesday.
A poet wrote on my wall. I kept the wall.
Room service, but honest. I am adding you to breakfast.
Unkind and correct. That is my department. Welcome to it.
{card}. It is exhausting, having a weakness. I used to have none.
Mr Brock, the chandelier is swinging. Please land.
Mr Brock, the chandelier asked to leave. I said no. You go instead.
Mr Brock. All four hundred stairs. Yours. I shall take the lift and watch.
templates: Absurd-scale dignitary or nation precedent: '[a bishop / duke / sultan / eleven kings / three governments / a coronation / a navy / a small country / two countries / a river / the sky] + flat aside' (19 lines). This was the round 2 fix; it is now the tic. Three governments appears twice (oneOnOne vex and pick vex), dukes twice. Exemplar kept: 'I have expensive taste. I once sent back a sunset. How do you keep up?'

Ban / relocate / remove as the button after a trivial offence (9 non-cut lines plus every cut by design). Exemplar kept: '{card}. I once had a bishop removed for that. He was mid-sentence.' 'And its parents' and 'Then remove the room' escalate past the target and are left out of the count, but note three of his best lines are this one joke.

oneOnOne: '[Name], I [own / have / keep / hosted] [N things]. [One-to-four-word question?]' (12 of 16 open on a possession or a count; 'Interested?' twice, 'Impressed?', 'Explain it', 'Convince me'). Only 'Mr Dash, I can see myself in your visor. I look wonderful. Keep still.' escapes the shape; the best of the template, 'Defend the shorts', is counted under the scale template.
Billing / invoice / deposit / charge as the button (8 lines). Exemplar kept: 'Short. Good. I bill by the word.'

Staff-count firing as a compliment: 'I have N [receptionists / chauffeurs / chefs / switchboard]. I am sacking them for you' (6 lines). Exemplar kept: 'I have fourteen chauffeurs. I am sacking thirteen.'
Henri as the last-clause imperative (6 lines, always the same slot). Exemplar kept: 'Nav, you are being relocated. Henri has a very long pole.'

Pick as '[Name]. I have [rebuilt / rewritten / moved / erased / bought / dismissed] [huge thing]. [Consequence].' (6 of 16 picks). Exemplar kept: 'Miss Tilly. I have had the suite rebuilt eighteen inches lower.'
'[Verdict]. Continue.' ruling (4 cardReact 'on' lines). Exemplar kept: 'That is how I talk to banks. Continue.'
Noted, not a template yet: the chandelier as a recurring prop (4 lines: Nav, Brock twice, the drama card) and Brock's stairs and 'I shall watch' (3 lines across oneOnOne and pick).
ruleBreaks: No line is over its word limit, no em dash, no emoji, no list, no exclamation mark, no contraction (only possessives), no 'as an AI', nothing beyond PG-13, no real person or brand.

Breaks the persona's own rule ('never build a line on what a suitor secretly fears or wants'; CAST.md secrets): 'Nav. I have had a lake erased from every map. You know the one.' / 'Nav, I once misplaced a wedding party in the spa. Ever lost one?' / 'Your Highness, your kingdom may be real. Your reservation is not.' / 'Your Highness. I checked your references. All real. I am mortified. The key is yours.' / 'Mr Dash. Late checkout. Indefinitely. Tell the dashboard whatever you like.'

Too nice for a star with standards (compliment with no cost or blade): 'She is wasted on a helpline. I am poaching her.' / 'I have fired forty receptionists looking for that voice.' / 'Miss Tilly, my staff would follow you into fire. Name your salary.' / 'Sir Quill, I own a room with a desk and a view. Interested?'
Cut that is too soft: 'Miss Tilly, I have a cupboard for lost umbrellas. You will be very comfortable.'
Borderline stock romance phrase, rescued by the turn but worth watching: 'Exact figures. I could kiss you. I shall invoice you.'

Near lift from the bar rather than a rule break: 'Good evening. It is exhausting, being the best thing in every room I own.' is Vera #45 ('such a chore being this beautiful') with a hotel noun, and the same opener recurs in 'It is exhausting, having a weakness. I used to have none.'
biggestGap: The absurd-scale precedent that fixed round 2 (a bishop, dukes, a sultan, eleven kings, three governments twice, a coronation, a navy, a small country, two countries, a river, the sky) now carries about 19 lines and every one of them is a boast about his own reach told in the same full-stop rhythm. Cut that device to its five best and refill the freed slots with Vera's other status move, a presumption about the suitor (he takes for granted that the suitor already works for him, owes him, or will obviously do the outrageous thing, as in 'You'd be willing to cover up the literal murder... Right?'), ending on a tag question or a bare order so the rhythm changes too.
bestLines: Put the fee on his room. Then remove the room.
Left, you say. Very well. The building will turn.
Mr Dash, you are blacklisted from every hotel I own. Which is most hotels.
Escalate me, Miss Tilly. Do. There is nobody above me.
Nav, a window on the ninth floor is open. It was not open before.

Vera (12, the corpus holds only about ten of her own lines, so narration about her fills the set): #12 'my career on not dating losers like you', #45 'such a chore being this beautiful all the time', #46 'the Cools over the Un-Cools', #47 'cover up the literal murder I've committed, no questions asked. Right?', #48 'Right. Now.', #49 'since you're SUCH a good advisor...', #50, #51 the feminism lecture that ends as an order, #52 the four drinks ending in poison, #56 the 50 Monster Dollars option, #53 and #55 narration. (a) Voice: ours. With names covered Maximilian is identifiable by shape alone: no contractions, 'I shall', 'Do.', formal address, a fragment then a procedural ruling. Several Vera lines (#50 'Come on, think of something!') are quest-hook filler any Monster Prom character says. (b) Construction: bar, narrowly, and the closest it has been. Our top twelve are as economical as hers and every one turns on its last words; nothing explains itself. But all twelve run the same rhythm (two or three full-stop fragments) and three of them are the same removal joke (the room, the joke's parents, the bishop). Vera's ten use at least five distinct constructions: the repeated-word fake-out (#12), the presumption that enlists the listener with a tag (#47), the complaint as boast (#45), the bare two-word order (#48), the escalating list that ends on poison (#52). Her presumptions also implicate the other person; nearly all of his are about his own reach. (c) Quotable: tie. 'The building will turn', 'Which is most hotels' and 'Then remove the room' clip as well as 'my career on not dating losers like you' and 'Right. Now.' Verdict: bar, on construction only. GENERIC COUNT: 74 of 191 (39%), down from 45% in round 2 and 48% in round 1. By section: intro 1/4, questions 5/12, react 16/48, cardReact 14/48, cut 4/16, twistIntro 2/12, ex 0/3, oneOnOne 15/16, hold 4/4, pick 9/16, reveal 4/9, outro 0/3. One exemplar of each template is kept out of the count. What improved since round 2: the 'wrong venue', 'nobody has ever [verb] me' and 'grant then forbid' templates are almost gone; cuts and per-suitor reacts now start from his world, and the cut section is the cleanest in the bank. What got worse: the scale precedent spread from 5 lines to about 19, oneOnOne became one shape (15 of 16 flagged, across the possession-plus-question, scale and staff-firing templates), and the hold section is now four templated lines out of four.
